stemMd: On a contour map, consecutive contours represent elevations 100 m, 110 m and 120 m. They are more closely spaced on the eastern slope than on the western slope. What does this indicate?

options.label: B
options.textMd: The contour interval changes only in the east

options.label: C
options.textMd: The eastern ground is necessarily higher at every point

options.label: E
options.textMd: The western slope has no elevation change

explanationMd: With a fixed vertical interval, closer contours mean that the same elevation change occurs over less horizontal distance. Rise divided by run is therefore larger in the east. Absolute elevation is read from labels rather than spacing alone.

distractorRationale.c: Spacing indicates gradient, not absolute height everywhere.
distractorRationale.b: The interval is explicitly ten metres throughout.
distractorRationale.e: Wide spacing still represents a change in elevation.
distractorRationale.d: The same rise occurs over a shorter horizontal distance.
